STRATEGY (15-minute and 1-minute candles)
Read on the previous day, the latest completed session (P). Candles are labelled by start time: the last candles are 15m 15:15 (second last 15:00) and 1m 15:29 (second last 15:28). A stock matches only when ALL of these hold:
1) 15m volume: the 15:00 candle's volume is higher than the 15:15 candle's.
2) 15m trend: the 15:00 and 15:15 candles have the same trend.
3) 1m volume: the 15:28 candle's volume is higher than the 15:29 candle's.
4) The 15m 15:00 and 1m 15:28 candles have the same trend.
5) The morning candles (09:15) of the 15m and 1m timeframes have that same trend too.
6) Previous day: the 15m 15:00 candle's trend is the same as the trend of the 15m 15:00 candle of the session before P.
The 1m timeframe has no same-trend rule on its last two candles (the report shows it for information only).
Trend = candle colour (close vs open); a flat candle has no trend, so it is never the same as another.
Data sources: every stock is scanned on NSE; every stock that does not pass there is also scanned on Yahoo for the same session. A stock that passes on either source is shown as a signal, tagged with the source(s) it passed on.
Direction follows the alignment trend (the second-last candles: 15m 15:00 / 1m 15:28): Up is LONG, Down is SHORT.
Entry: the 09:15 open on entry day. Exit: 15:27.

Data notes: candles come from the primary source (NSE - the DATA_SOURCE setting) with Yahoo as the fallback and second source; the source of each stock is shown in the Data column. NSE's charting feed supplies 1-minute candles, and the 15-minute candles are built from them on a 09:15 grid (open = first, close = last, volume = sum); a stock read from Yahoo uses Yahoo's own 15-minute and 1-minute feeds. Prices are rounded to 2 decimals; zero-volume and corrupt candles are dropped and count as missing, which can only block a match. DATA CONFLICT means a native 15m candle's trend, or which 15m candle has more volume, disagrees with the same candles rebuilt from the 1m candles inside them, so the symbol is blocked rather than trusted. INCOMPLETE means no completed session (or none of the seven candles) came back. STALE means the session read, or the session before it, differs from most other symbols. Each candle is shown as open→close with its volume so a signal can be checked against a chart.
